summary: This function takes a list of node names and generates a Mermaid flowchart diagram where each node flows left-to-right into the next one. It formats the output as a Mermaid code block so that Quarto (a document processing tool) will render it as a visual diagram.

explanations.4: enumerate() gives us both the position (i) and the actual name from the list, so we can number our nodes and use their names as labels.
explanations.5: We're building a Mermaid syntax string that creates a node with a unique identifier (node0, node1, etc.) and displays the actual name inside square brackets.
explanations.6: We skip creating an arrow for the very first node since there's nothing before it to connect from.
explanations.7: This creates an arrow in Mermaid syntax that points from the previous node to the current node, forming the chain.
explanations.10: The triple backticks with {mermaid} is special Quarto syntax that tells it to interpret the following block as a Mermaid diagram rather than plain text.
